# NBAPI 1.5.0

## Upstream integration

- Rebased NBAPI onto the latest upstream `v1.0.0-rc.22` release published on 2026-07-26.
- Added upstream model discovery for Codex-compatible and advanced custom channels.
- Added Sub2API, alpha-search billing, configurable tool pricing, current Gemini image models, and OpenAI Realtime GA routing.
- Integrated the latest pricing, subscription, quota, user-management, task-refund, streaming, proxy, and administration fixes from upstream `rc.17` through `rc.22`.
- Included the upstream fix that prevents duplicate tool calls in Responses-to-Chat streaming.

## NBAPI compatibility

- Preserved automatic Moonshot `/v1/responses` to ChatCompletions conversion and its unsupported-tool filtering.
- Preserved the per-channel option that forces every Responses request through ChatCompletions conversion.
- Preserved loose and strict Responses tool conversion policies, custom `/v1` and `/v3` base-path routing, HA management, operations monitoring, channel UI, OAuth callback helpers, and subscription quota administration.
- Kept compatibility-sensitive legacy authentication headers, token issuers, cookie names, and browser storage keys so existing sessions and clients continue to work after upgrade.

## Frontend

- Completed the planned removal of the Classic frontend source and build pipeline.
- Kept the NBAPI Default frontend as the only bundled web interface.
- Migrated NBAPI-specific channel, HA, subscription, OAuth, update, branding, and system-information UI into the latest frontend structure.

## Deployment and pricing

- Replaced the development-oriented Compose variants with one production `docker-compose.yml` that always pulls `ghcr.io/lorry-san/nbapi:latest`.
- Added required PostgreSQL, Redis, session, and encryption secrets, persistent Redis storage, and service health checks.
- Updated production setup instructions to generate four independent UUID secrets in `.env`.
- Added OpenRouter `input_cache_write` import support and maps it to NBAPI's `create_cache_ratio`.

## Upgrade notes

- Back up the database and current environment before upgrading.
- Existing PostgreSQL data volumes retain the password stored at initial database creation. Changing only `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in `.env` does not update that stored password.
- Classic is no longer included. Installations that still select Classic will be served by the Default frontend compatibility path.
